newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares tumble at outset of bourse dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares tumble at outset of bourse dealings.

text.p: Germany's DAX index tumbled more than one percent in early bourse dealings on Thursday, hurt by overnight Wall Street losses and profit-taking after the blue-chip index raced to record highs in the last week.
Dealers said the DAX would likely consolidate between 3,900 and 4,000 points after seven consecutive record-setting bourse sessions.
The 30-share DAX was down 58.37 points at 3,997.49 points, while the IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was down 30.61 points at 3,996.36 points.
Traders said the strong dollar, which was trading above 1.76 marks in morning European dealings on Thursday, would underpin the market against heavy losses.
"It is rather healthy to have a small correction," one trader said, adding the market was not too worried about recent swings in the Dow Jones Index.

With little corporate news scheduled on Thursday, traders said the market may focus on the Bundesbank news conference scheduled for 1015 GMT following its annual out-of-town council meeting in Aschau, southern Germany.
Traders expect the central bank to leave rates unchanged at the meeting but will be looking for comments from council members on the dollar's strong gains and the economic outlook.

Among specific shares, electronics group Siemens AG was the most heavily traded stock in early business after saying late on Wednesday it had formed an alliance with computer networking group 3Com Corp to jointly market and develop voice and data networking products.
Siemens shares were up 1.15 marks in morning trade to 110.75 but then fell 45 pfennigs to 109.85 marks.
Building group Bilfinger + Berger Bau AG was steady at 78 marks after saying its 1997 group output climbed three percent to 9.52 billion marks.
Insurance group Allianz AG was down in line with the market despite saying at its annual general meeting that it expected group premium income to rise 11 percent in 1997.
